scope: Jinsongbei Community (Chaoyang, Beijing) organic renewal and smart governance: case boundary, inclusion/exclusion criteria, research questions

candidates.content: Case name: Jinsongbei Community organic renewal and smart governance pilot, Chaoyang, Beijing
Period 2018-07 to 2023-12; core implementation 2018-07 to 2022-12; 2023 as follow-up observation
Core space limited to Jinsongbei Community (Jinsong Blocks 1-2); Blocks 3-8 only as agreement scope and diffusion context

Include six core processes: partnership and diagnosis; demonstration-area construction; property entry; fee collection and property-plus-eldercare; smart/age-friendly equipment; best-practice recognition and operation
Exclude other Jinsong blocks, other community cases, national policy, and generic industry technology claims
Five research questions: micro-profit closure; five-party participation; technology-capability-action inventory; smart renewal as goal/tool/narrative; sustainability
Treat smart governance as a parallel theme with a higher evidence threshold; do not presume a system-level smart-governance regime
Record stair-climbing machines, electric wheelchairs, emergency callers, and grab bars first as age-friendly technology/services; whether to classify them as smart governance remains open

conflicts: Household counts: 3605 project households vs 4199 community households vs 3684 in community profiles
Investment: RMB 30 million at 45% of total (T03) vs total about RMB 290 million and 200,000 sqm (T10); possibly phase vs full project
Property-fee collection: 60% in June 2020 (T06) vs 75% in November 2020 (T04), a time series with unclear scope
Demonstration-area completion: official 2019-08-02 vs some media 2019-09
Property entry: T05 points to June 2019; other sources say 2019 or 2020
HEDATA platform deployment is a corporate claim without independent verification of functions, coverage, or usage
Face recognition (T05) and smart access control (T07) may be the same device or different batches
Demonstration area is about 10% of Blocks 1-2, not the whole community
T07 reports 9 stair-climbing machines and 12 electric wheelchairs for 'Jinsong community', possibly across multiple sub-communities, not Jinsongbei alone
decisions_required: Time boundary: A 2018-07 to 2022-12 / B 2018-07 to 2023-12 with follow-up (recommended) / C 2018-07 to 2026-11
Limit core space to Jinsongbei Community (Blocks 1-2), with Blocks 3-8 only as context? (recommended yes)
Theme structure: organic renewal as primary and smart governance as a parallel, evidence-gated sub-theme? (recommended yes)
Classify stair-climbing machines, wheelchairs, callers, and grab bars as age-friendly services rather than smart governance? (recommended yes)
Adopt the five draft research questions? Add privacy/data governance and resident acceptance as separate questions?

history_impact.note: C14 shares a Chinese urban-community renewal context with C04 and C05; check their social-capital, property, and smart-technology concept boundaries during later comparison.
